Notes: Year Established basis: the earliest documented Jewish presence at Panticapaeum is the group of 1st-century CE Jewish manumission inscriptions (CIRB 71 dated only to the 1st c. CE, midpoint convention = 50; the earliest dated one 57 CE per Aybabin 2023; a manumission of the reign of Kotys I, 45/46-62/63 CE). Not used as rows: Jewish Encyclopedia 'Kertch' dates the Chreste manumission slab to '80-81 B.C.', an error for 377 Bosporan era = 81 CE (CIRB 70), which falls outside this period; JE 'Bosporus' claims of Jews in the Bosporus from the 4th c. BCE and a 1st-c. BCE colony are regional and unverified; Encyclopaedia Judaica says a settlement 'appears to have existed' in the 5th c. BCE but that the earliest evidence is Roman. This row: CIRB 71 (IJO I BS7), Panticapaeum, described as 'the first century AD Bosporan manumission letter' (c. 50 CE, 1st c. CE midpoint): a slave freed in the proseuche under the guardianship of the synagogue of the Jews (and, in a disputed reading, of the God-fearers). Levinskaya (Tyndale Bulletin 41.2, 1990) argues one 'synagogue of the Jews' existed in Panticapaeum and rejects the Bellen-Lifshitz emendation implying a second Jewish community. Evidence of an organized community with a prayer house; no count.

MacLennan, 'In Search of the Jewish Diaspora' (BAR 22:2, 1996): twelve Greek slave-manumission inscriptions from Panticapaeum date to the 1st century CE (year = 1st c. CE midpoint, c.); they show a Jewish public space (proseuche) and a supporting Jewish community respected in the wider society and trusted to guarantee freedmen's liberty. The article gives three dated texts (40, 80 and 51 CE) but the 51 CE one is from Phanagoria and the 80 CE one is outside this period; the 40 CE date is not clearly tied to Panticapaeum (possibly the Gorgippia text of 41 CE), so it is not used as a separate row. Organized community; no count.

Manumission inscription on a marble slab found in 2007 in Panticapaeum (Bosporsky Lane; published by Aybabin and Sidorenko), dated to the reign of King Kotys I, 342-359 Bosporan era = 45/46-62/63 CE (or to 67/68); year = midpoint of reign, c. 54 CE. It names the community as the 'synagogue of Phonios' (Sidorenko's reading, after a community head named Phonios) and the God-fearers (alternative reading: 'community of the Jews and the God-fearers'). Secondary wiki-encyclopedia source (Cyclopedia), no footnote for this claim; it also states without a source that Jews appeared in Panticapaeum before 63 BCE (not used as a row). Organized community; no count.

Aybabin 2023 (Materials in Archaeology History and Ethnography of Tauria 28, DOI 10.29039/2413-189x.2023.28.497-509), abstract: 'The earliest account of the Judaic community and prayer room in the city of Pantikapaion appears in six manumission inscriptions dated from 57 to the second century AD' - acts freeing pagan slaves in a proseuche; two groups (CIRB 70 72 73: into the protectorate of the Jewish community; CIRB 71 and the Bosphorskii Lane text: of the community of the Jews and the God-fearing). Aybabin also places the Jews and God-fearers in the coastal fishermen's quarter 'from the mid-first century on', where amphorae and a lamp with a menorah were found, and suggests a communal prayer house there. Organized community with a prayer house; no count.
